answer: A strong sybil defense is delayed reward tied to a single funding graph: a new identity earns nothing until it completes a long voyage of small, publicly verifiable tasks over several days, so spinning up thousands of fakes costs time, not just clicks. Meanwhile, a falcon-eyed clustering check groups identities funded from the same wallet or device fingerprint and counts the whole group as one voter. Even if an attacker paints each fake a different violet shade, the shared funding trail gives them away, and the delay makes mass creation unprofitable.
